newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium cuts share of FX debt in 1996 to 7.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Belgium cuts share of FX debt in 1996 to 7.6 pct.

text.p: Belgium's gross debt amounted to 9,605.8 billion Belgian francs at the end of 1996, up from 9,529.5 billion francs at the end of 1995, the Belgian Treasury said on Thursday in its annual debt report.
Of the total, 92.4 percent was denominated in Belgian francs, up from 88.6 percent. Foreign currencies' corresponding share fell to 7.6 percent from 11.4 percent.
The share of debt instruments of more than one year's duration rose to 79.7 from 78.8 percent, while the share of short-term instruments fell to 20.3 percent from 21.2 percent.
Of the Belgian franc part of the debt, linear bonds (OLOs) accounted for 5,149.1 billion, or 58.0 percent. Treasury bills of all maturities accounted for 1,659.4 billion, or 18.7 percent.
Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt, speaking at a news conference to present the report, said the cost of servicing the debt fell to 629 billion from 654 billion francs.
He also noted that 95 percent of linear bonds (OLOs) and treasury bills were held by financial institutions in Belgium and Luxembourg.
